verdict_text:
YES

The script drops exactly the 12 `h.<i>.attn.bias` buffers via a `fullmatch` that cannot also hit `h.<i>.attn.c_attn.bias`, casts exactly the 48 listed projection matrices with `.to(torch.bfloat16)` (round-to-nearest-even), leaves every other tensor as untouched float32 under its original name, and asserts all four required checks before any write. The sharding is greedy in iteration order with a flush whenever adding a tensor would exceed 67,108,864 bytes of tensor data, so no shard exceeds the limit and an oversized tensor such as `wte.weight` necessarily lands alone (any following tensor forces a flush because the running size already exceeds the cap), and the index file's `weight_map` covers all 148 tensors.
